summary.oneLiner: Fabtech delivered 28% revenue growth in FY26 driven by GCC/Africa expansion, though margins compressed due to mix and logistics; the ₹230cr IPO reset the balance sheet, enabling a shift from survival to scaling with a record ₹900cr order book guiding 25-30% growth.

one-line thesis: Fabtech delivered 28% revenue growth in FY26 driven by GCC/Africa expansion, though margins compressed due to mix and logistics; the ₹230cr IPO reset the balance sheet, enabling a shift from survival to scaling with a record ₹900cr order book guiding 25-30% growth.
financial scorecard: Revenue ₹431.3cr (+28.4% YoY); EBITDA ₹55.6cr (+18.3%, margin ~12.9% vs ~14% prior); PAT ₹38.4cr (reported, down from ₹46.5cr due to ₹17.8cr exceptional item in FY25; normalized operational PAT ₹36.6cr +17.4%); Order Book >₹900cr; Net Debt reduced to ₹42cr from ₹54cr despite USD loans; One-offs: FY25 had ₹17.85cr exceptional gain (TSA), FY26 had ₹1.77cr exceptional cost.
guidance: Revenue growth 25-30%; PAT margin target 9.9%-10.5%; Order inflow pipeline ~$200mn (hot leads); Capex focused on talent acquisition and JV deployment rather than heavy asset buildup.
order book & pipeline: >₹900cr providing 18-24 months visibility; Geographic split: UAE (largest), Saudi, Kenya, North/West Africa; Ticket sizes increased from $30-40mn to $70mn; Conversion rate improving from 11% to 16-17% of hot leads.
segment / subsidiary detail: Core pharma turnkey (greenfield/brownfield); New entries in Animal Health/Veterinary vaccines; Medical devices; Integration of PEB and solar into offerings; In-house manufacturing for process equipment, containment, partitions, water, air.
growth verticals / optionality: Africa corridor (Kenya momentum); GCC localization mandates driving local subsidiary wins; Moving up value chain to oncology/vaccines via FABL JV; Hybrid solutions (PEB+Solar) increasing ticket size and controlling timelines.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin pressure from portfolio mix (higher Africa volume @ lower margins) and logistics/freight costs due to geopolitical disruption; RMC costs rose faster than revenue; Mitigation via variation clauses in contracts and USD billing hedging local currency risk.
capex / expansion: Light asset model; IPO proceeds deployed for talent acquisition, working capital (via monitoring account), and strategic JVs/acquisitions (due diligence ongoing for West acquisition); No heavy greenfield manufacturing capex mentioned.
capital allocation: Prioritizing working capital efficiency (receivables mgmt critical at ₹204cr); Debt reduction (USD loans retained for arbitrage); Strategic equity infusions for local subsidiaries; Evaluating M&A for capability gaps.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical instability in Middle East affecting logistics/visas; Receivables bloating (₹204cr) impacting cash conversion; Execution delays due to client civil readiness; Raw material cost inflation; Currency devaluation in African markets (mitigated by USD billing).
management quality / tone: Confident on structural transformation and long-term scale; Acknowledges margin headwinds as temporary mix/logistics issues; Emphasizes 'not a quarter-to-quarter story' due to lumpy billing; Focused on cash collection and execution discipline.
non-obvious takeaways: Revenue recognition strictly tied to Bill of Lading against LCs causing lumpiness; Retention of USD debt despite cash surplus due to favorable interest arbitrage (>200 bps benefit); Shift to Executive Chairman role to separate strategy from execution; Variation clauses allow price renegotiation post-detailed engineering.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Flagship of the Fabtech Group, positioned as a start-to-finish turnkey solutions provider to life sciences and healthcare, integrating design, engineering, manufacturing, installation and validation under a single accountable partner to eliminate vendor coordination risk.
- Claims three decades of engineering excellence and a footprint spanning 62 countries (60+ across 6 continents), building GMP-compliant, energy-efficient and contamination-controlled environments.
- Regulatory credentialing is framed as the moat: a unified turnkey approach is presented as ensuring every system meets global cGMP, WHO, EU-GMP, USFDA and ISO standards from first blueprint to final validation.
- Heavily geared to the MEA pharmaceutical self-reliance theme post-COVID, with 78% of revenue from MENA, GCC and ECO Zone markets and international revenue share of roughly 55%.
- Chairman frames the aspiration as becoming stronger, more resilient and a global benchmark in life sciences engineering rather than simply larger.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order book] Open order book of ₹900+ Cr as of June 30, 2026 with stated visibility over the next two years, against active enquiries of ₹9,300+ Cr and hot leads of ₹3,800+ Cr.
- [Geopolitics] Geopolitics has temporarily delayed finalisation of certain orders, but the deck states there have been no cancellations and customer engagement remains highly active.
- [Industry tailwinds] Cited demand drivers are accelerating biologics and specialty pharma capex, GCC and Africa healthcare infrastructure investment, regulatory pressure driving global facility upgrades, and China+1 manufacturing diversification.
- [Repeat business] Repeat clients accounted for ₹8.4 Cr of Q1 FY27 order inflows of ₹96.5 Cr, a low repeat share relative to total inflows.
